clue.text: Turned up carrying a bit of food amid havoc, offering assistance

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: havoc or chaos is hell

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the following word is read backwards
amid means in the middle of, so the built piece goes inside the havoc word

parts.note: taken as written, then turned to PU

indicators.note: only a small bit is wanted, here the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter of food

explanation.surface: Someone arrives clutching a snack in the middle of chaos and offers to help.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the turned-up word swallows the food letter, and that whole unit then sits inside the havoc word.
explanation.definitionFit: Helpful describes a person or thing that gives aid, the same as offering assistance.

clue.text: Travelling salesman: he works with trucks

indicators.note: works suggests something being worked or processed into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a door-to-door salesman who does his job out of lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: A huckster is a hawker or pedlar who sells goods on the road, a travelling seller.

clue.text: Drink mate overturned

indicators.note: overturned means upside down, so in a down entry the word runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: A friend's glass gets knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap is to drink by scooping up liquid with the tongue, as a cat does.

clue.text: Tree's end of life? Axe

parts.note: a fir is a tree

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: last letter of life

explanation.surface: Is the axe what ends a tree's life?
explanation.walkthrough: Axe looks like the tool that fells the tree, but it is the verb meaning sack.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone and to axe them both mean to dismiss them from a job.

clue.text: Student name included in revival of matinee feature

indicators.note: being included in something places these letters inside it
a revival is a new production, so the letters are staged again in another order

parts.note: L for learner, a student
N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drama student gets a credit in a revived afternoon performance of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: L and N go into the jumble of matinee's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineament is a distinctive line or contour of the face, so a facial feature.

clue.text: Item of church furniture and other things brought back, secured by the French navy

indicators.note: something secured by others is held fast between them, so it goes inside

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the abbreviation is read right to left

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and other things
Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A church inventory lists a fixture and sundries, all shipped home under guard by the French navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The French and navy are two separate pieces that together hold the reversed abbreviation between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is the stand in a church from which the Bible is read.

clue.text: Minor difficulty with power cut

indicators.note: cut means taken away, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a plight is a difficult situation
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A small inconvenience: the electricity has been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: Minor difficulty reads as one phrase, but Minor is the definition alone; PLIGHT loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Light means trivial or not serious, as in a light sentence, so minor.

clue.text: English writer's trunk initially received in English school

parts.note: a trunk is a chest, the box or the torso

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the school's name

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: first letter of received

explanation.surface: An English author's luggage first turned up at a boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link joining definition to wordplay. Eton College is England's best-known boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: G K Chesterton was the English author of the Father Brown detective stories.

clue.text: Consume fuel without pressure

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is left out of the word

parts.note: peat is burnt as fuel
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: An engine burning fuel without any pressure building up.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat something is to consume it as food.

clue.text: One day in tabloid elevated male page 3 behaviour?

indicators.note: elevated means raised up, so in a down entry the letters are read from the bottom
in puts the first pieces inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
I is the Roman numeral one
D is the abbreviation for day
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: One day a man appeared on page 3 of a tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 of The Sun famously featured topless models, so the definition plays on the very paper used in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudism is going about unclothed, which is what Sun page 3 models were known for.

clue.text: Holidaymaker losing money in scam?

indicators.note: losing something means it drops out, so one letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a camper is someone on a camping holiday
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A tourist gets fleeced by a con and is left out of pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMPER without its M leaves CAPER. The question mark flags that a caper is only loosely a scam.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a slang word for a crafty or illegal escapade, so a scheme or swindle.

clue.text: Decent leg breaks not deployed

indicators.note: when something breaks it falls apart and the pieces can be put back in any order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a bowler's tidy leg-breaks go unused because the captain never brings him on.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg breaks are spinning deliveries in cricket, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neglected has been left unused or ignored, just as a resource not deployed sits idle.

clue.text: Premiere ignoring latest top performer

indicators.note: the latest letter is the last one, and ignoring it means leaving it off

parts.note: a premiere is the start of a show's run

explanation.surface: At a film premiere the leading actor skips the newest gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: START with its final T dropped leaves STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is the leading or most celebrated performer in a show or field.

clue.text: Dirigible excellent? A tear? Keeping quiet

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the tear word wraps around the call for silence

parts.note: a tear is a rip
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Questions about a blimp: is it splendid, or has it sprung a leak, and is it being kept hush-hush?
explanation.walkthrough: A1 for first-class is often written AI in crosswords. The A of A tear only serves the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible is a steerable lighter-than-air craft, which is an airship.

clue.text: Quarrelling about it, dismissing rule as contrived

indicators.note: dismissing sends something away, so that letter is taken out
about means around, so the word wraps itself round the short piece

parts.note: fractious means irritable and quarrelsome
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: People bickering over a regulation and throwing it out as artificial.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarrelling suggests a verb, but it is the adjective sense, as in quarrelling children.
explanation.definitionFit: Factitious means artificially made up or not genuine, exactly what contrived means.

clue.text: Surplus quantity? Broadcasting including extremely reduced sport

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the broadcast word wraps around the rest

parts.note: a programme being broadcast is on

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the last letter of the intensifier is lost

parts.note: very means extremely
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A TV schedule running late because a cut-down sports programme overran.
explanation.walkthrough: Reduced applies to extremely, not to the sport. RU for rugby union is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An overrun is an amount by which something exceeds its allowance, such as a cost overrun.

clue.text: Criminal organisation represented in cartoons about South America

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the region's abbreviation
represented means shown again in another form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
SA is the abbreviation for South America

explanation.surface: A gang portrayed in comic strips set in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Cartoons rearranged gives CONOSTRA, which wraps around SA after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosa Nostra is the name for the Sicilian and American Mafia, an organised crime syndicate.

clue.text: Location for personal decoration displaying British honourees

parts.note: an earl holds a British peerage, one kind of honour
an OBE is an Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A spot where personal medals or decorations are shown off by British dignitaries.
explanation.walkthrough: One plural phrase covers two different honourees, a peer and a member of an order, set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The earlobe is where earrings are worn, a place for adorning oneself.

clue.text: Depressing sound from electronic network going over

indicators.note: something going over flips across, so the network word is read backwards

parts.note: a grid is a network, such as the electricity grid
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A gloomy hum coming from the electricity network as it fails.
explanation.walkthrough: GRID read backwards is DIRG, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow mournful song or lament, a sad and depressing piece of music.

clue.text: Disorder in internal plumbing? Start to develop repairs to pipes, say

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is used

parts.note: first letter of develop

indicators.note: repairs rework something into a new state, so the letters are put together afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plumbing fault inside the house starts to develop, so the pipes need fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: Say looks like a casual aside meaning for example, but it is part of the anagram letters. Internal plumbing is a joke for the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is indigestion, a disorder of the digestive tract, playfully called internal plumbing.

clue.text: Rock group in church regarding unknown service

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
R.E.M. is an American rock band
on means about or regarding
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A band plays in a church at a service for someone unnamed.
explanation.walkthrough: In is only a link here, not a container signal. R.E.M. is an American rock band; Y is an algebraic unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremony is a formal religious or public rite, which is one sense of service.

clue.text: Compassion and passion may be about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: heat is intensity of feeling, passion
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A thought on feelings: kindness and ardour might be the correct way to be.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAT goes around R: HE-R-AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart is used for kindness and sympathy, as in having a heart, which is compassion.

clue.text: Special valour, ousting a tyrant

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special

indicators.note: ousting throws someone out, so the letter named after it is removed

parts.note: valour is courage
the letter that is thrown out

explanation.surface: Heroic special forces overthrow a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: The a reads as the article before tyrant, but it is the letter taken out of the valour word.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a cruel oppressor or source of affliction, so a tyrant fits.

clue.text: Book getting support after admitting a boob?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the support word takes the letter inside

parts.note: a rest is a support, as in an armrest
taken as written

explanation.surface: A book gets endorsed after its author admits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside REST to make REAST, after B. Boob looks like a mistake but here is slang for a breast.
explanation.definitionFit: Boob is informal slang for a woman's breast; the question mark flags the slang.

clue.text: Showed pain after modern version criticised

indicators.note: after places the pain phrase behind the version phrase, so the second-read piece comes first

parts.note: a repro is a reproduction, a modern copy of an antique
to ache is to show or feel pain

explanation.surface: Someone winced at a remake and then slated it.
explanation.walkthrough: After means the pain word comes second, though it is read first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to rebuke or find fault with them, which is to criticise.

clue.text: Sound triumphant over new coin

parts.note: to crow is to boast loudly about a victory
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone gloats over a freshly minted coin.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, over places the first piece above the second. A crown was an old British coin worth five shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown is a British coin, historically worth five shillings and now issued for commemorations.

clue.text: Some seen kerb-crawling around joint

indicators.note: crawling around turns back on itself, so the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
some means only part of the text, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: the letters running across these two words

explanation.surface: Some people have been spotted kerb-crawling around a seedy club.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerb-crawling, cruising slowly to pick up a prostitute, hides the reversal signal; read backwards from k in kerb into seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge between thigh and shin, one of the body's joints.

clue.text: Mostly difficult for one to enter — locks?

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the numeral slips into the shortened word
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: hard means difficult
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: It's mostly hard for anyone to get in: are the doors locked?
explanation.walkthrough: HARD without its D is HAR, and I goes inside. Locks looks like door fastenings, but means tresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks are tresses or strands of hair on the head.

clue.text: Good sporting outcome: cricketer getting runs amidst a defeat

indicators.note: amidst means in the middle of, so the player and runs go inside

parts.note: a defeat is a loss
a bat is a batsman
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman piling up runs while his side still loses, yet the result is good.
explanation.walkthrough: BAT plus R goes inside A LOSS. The cricket surface hides a golf definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an albatross is a hole played three under par, an excellent score.

clue.text: Excluding lawyers?

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a question about shutting out the legal profession; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a preposition meaning except and as the collective name for barristers.

clue.text: Silver band not in prominent position, causing difficulties

indicators.note: a prominent position is one high up, and not being there means that two-letter word is taken away

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: A brass band relegated to the back row, causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Up means prominent or raised, so a band not in prominent position is the band word without its up.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for trouble, hassle or aggressive behaviour, so difficulties.

clue.text: Set on rising

indicators.note: rising goes upwards, so in a down entry the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A bare instruction to set something going upward.
explanation.walkthrough: On is a cricket term: the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to set firm, as jelly does.

clue.text: Mistake linked to area in output of Cornish mining country

indicators.note: in places the joined pieces inside the metal word

parts.note: tin was the main product of Cornwall's mines
to err is to make a mistake
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A blunder tied to the district where Cornish mining happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall, in south-west England, was famous for its tin mines. Country is the definition, meaning land rather than nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, the sense of country as in open country.

clue.text: Number of broadcasts? Pair arranged bet

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
to lay is to wager, as in lay a bet

explanation.surface: A punter asks how often something is broadcast, then places a fixed wager on a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' could suggest a song, and indeed a song's airplay counts how often it is broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Airplay is the amount of radio or TV play a record receives, so a count of its broadcasts.
